do: Ensure text has a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against its background for normal text
Ensure large text (18pt/24px or 14pt/19px bold) has a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against its background
Test all text colors against their actual rendered background colors, including gradients
Use contrast checking tools to verify ratios meet WCAG requirements (WebAIM, Stark, Deque, etc.)
Calculate contrast using the WCAG formula: (L1 + 0.05) / (L2 + 0.05) where L1 is lighter luminance
Test contrast in both light and dark mode themes if your application supports them
Verify contrast ratios for text over background images by testing against darkest/lightest areas
Ensure hover and focus states maintain sufficient contrast ratios
Test contrast on high-DPI displays and various device screen sizes
Use relative luminance calculation based on sRGB color space values
Test text contrast in different browser rendering modes (with/without font smoothing)
Verify contrast for dynamic content that changes color based on user interaction
Test link text contrast in both visited and unvisited states
Ensure error messages and validation text meet contrast requirements
Test button text contrast against button background colors including gradients
Verify placeholder text contrast meets requirements (avoid using placeholder as sole label)
Test contrast for text within custom UI components like tabs, accordions, and modals
Use automated testing tools (axe-core, WAVE) to catch obvious contrast failures
Perform manual testing for complex backgrounds and edge cases
Document color palettes with their contrast ratios for design system consistency
Specify both text and background colors explicitly (don’t rely on defaults)
On state changes (like hover, focus, active), maintain or increase contrast
Ensure text and images of text have a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 against their background (unless exempt)
Provide sufficient contrast for placeholder text, hover text, and focus text too (if visible)
Ensure visual indicators (e.g., focus outlines, selected states) meet at least 3:1 contrast with adjacent colors
When gradients or background images are used behind text, ensure the contrast holds across the background
dont: Do not rely solely on visual inspection - always use contrast calculation tools
Do not assume that dark text on light backgrounds automatically passes (e.g., #777777 on white fails)
Do not round up contrast ratios - 4.49:1 does not meet the 4.5:1 requirement
Do not forget to specify both foreground and background colors in CSS (F24 failure)
Do not use text over background images without ensuring adequate contrast throughout (F83 failure)
Do not rely on browser default colors - always specify both text and background colors
Do not assume OS-level high contrast settings meet WCAG requirements
Do not use color alone to convey information critical to understanding
Do not forget to test contrast in different user-selected themes or modes
Do not overlook contrast requirements for form validation messages and error text
Do not assume that larger font sizes automatically have better contrast perception
Do not use transparent backgrounds without considering the underlying content
Do not rely on CSS filters or opacity to achieve contrast - test the final rendered result
Do not ignore contrast requirements for interactive states (hover, focus, active)
Do not use automatic color generation without contrast verification
Do not assume that complementary colors have good contrast
Do not forget to test contrast on actual devices, not just desktop browsers
Do not use pure red text on pure green backgrounds or similar problematic combinations
Do not rely on bold or italic styling alone to meet contrast requirements
Do not ignore contrast testing for dynamically generated content
Do not use low-contrast colors (e.g., light grey on white) for body text or important labels
Do not assume an element is exempt when it still conveys meaningful information
Do not let contrast fall below the threshold on responsiveness or theming
Do not leave controls or icons without sufficient contrast, even if they are small or decorative
edge_cases: Text over gradient backgrounds: Test contrast against both lightest and darkest parts of gradient
Text over complex background images: Test against areas where text actually appears
Dynamic theming: Test contrast ratios in all available theme variations (light/dark/high-contrast)
Transparent overlays: Calculate final rendered colors including transparency effects
Text with CSS shadows or outlines: Consider shadow/outline contribution to contrast perception
Mobile responsive designs: Test contrast on various screen sizes and pixel densities
Text within SVG graphics: Ensure programmatic color values meet contrast requirements
Animated or transitioning colors: Verify contrast requirements are met throughout animation
Text over video backgrounds: Provide sufficient contrast or alternative overlay solutions
Custom font rendering: Test with various font-smoothing and anti-aliasing settings
Print stylesheets: Ensure contrast works for both screen and print media
High-DPI displays: Test that contrast calculations account for different pixel densities
Text selection colors: Ensure selected text maintains readable contrast ratios
Disabled form elements: While exempt, consider user experience for partially disabled states
Link text within paragraphs: Ensure sufficient contrast for both visited/unvisited states
Text over pattern backgrounds: Test against dominant colors in repetitive patterns
Color-shifted displays: Consider how contrast appears on different monitor calibrations
Text in data visualizations: Ensure chart labels meet contrast requirements against backgrounds
Modal dialog overlays: Test text contrast against both modal background and underlying content
Notification banners: Test contrast for temporary messaging overlays
Progressive web app themes: Test contrast in browser-managed theme environments
Text within iframes: Ensure contrast requirements are met in embedded content
CSS-generated content: Test contrast for ::before and ::after pseudo-element text
Text within canvas elements: Verify programmatic color combinations meet requirements
Thin or light-weight fonts: Even if numerical contrast passes, thin strokes may still be hard to read
Hover and focus overlays: UI overlays or shadows might reduce contrast — evaluate after effect
Inactive UI components (disabled buttons): May be exempt, but ensure legibility where possible
Subpixel rendering / anti-aliasing may reduce effective contrast; design with margin
techniques: G18: Ensuring that a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 exists between text and background
G145: Ensuring that a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 exists between text and background for large text
G174: Providing a control with a sufficient contrast ratio that allows users to switch to a presentation with sufficient contrast
SL13: Providing A Style Switcher To Switch To High Contrast
G148: Not specifying default colors (text or background) such that user agent styles may change contrast unexpectedly
G195: Ensuring non-text contrast (UI controls, focus indicators) provide at least 3:1 contrast with adjacent colors
axe_rules_hint: color-contrast: Ensures elements meet minimum color contrast ratio thresholds
color-contrast-enhanced: Ensures elements meet enhanced color contrast ratio thresholds (AAA level)
non-text-contrast: Checks that UI components and graphical objects meet minimum contrast requirements
focus-contrast: Ensures focus indicators are sufficiently contrasted
css-color-contrast: Detects CSS color declarations that cause low contrast
Text color does not have sufficient contrast against background, especially on gradients or images.
Interactive states such as hover or focus reduce contrast temporarily.
Dynamic themes or light/dark modes alter color combinations without rechecking contrast ratios.
Semi-transparent overlays or animations change visibility during user interaction.
Automation may report color contrast based on static snapshots and miss time-based variations.
Contrast evaluation in different viewport sizes and zoom levels.
